newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-SINGH, PRICE AND ELS TO BATTLE FOR SA OPEN CROWN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SINGH, PRICE AND ELS TO BATTLE FOR SA OPEN CROWN.

text.p: Fiji's Vijay Singh overpowered Glendower golf course with a second successive 66 to take a two-shot lead over Nick Price going into the final round of the 3.4 million rand (745,000 dollar) South African Open.

Singh's length off the tee enabled him to attack all four par fives with ease but he also displayed a silken touch around the greens, nowhere more obviously than on the 18th where he holed a slippery 15-foot putt for birdie.
"I have always been a mediocre putter but this week I've been putting better than for a very long time. If I can just keep it going I have a good chance of victory," Singh said afterwards.

Price, too, admitted to putting as well as he has done for a couple of years, producing seven birdies as well as a couple of tricky saves in a round of 65. He did not drop a shot all day and produced a tournament best back nine of 31.

Zimbabwean Price also offered an altogether unexpected reason for his success. "I was with our cricket side last night when they beat India just up the road in Centurion. I was completely inspired by them. That's why I wore one of their caps. I said I would if they won, and I'm chuffed for them. I'm horribly cricket-starved in the US."
Defending champion Ernie Els will complete an illustrious last day three-ball after carding a 67 for a three round total of 205, two behind Price and four behind Singh.

"I'm going to have to find something very, very special tomorrow to have a chance. Maybe a 64 will do it. I love playing with Nick so at least I'll be relaxed, and if you guys (the media) can remind Vijay of last year's World Matchplay final then maybe I'll have a chance!" Els told reporters.
But Singh was not rattled. "That was last year," he laughed when told of Els' comment. "This is a different tournament and we're both playing differently. It should be an exciting last day."

Price's fellow Zimbawean Mark McNulty, a three-time winner on the South African circuit already this year, is the only other man to have a realistic chance of victory after posting a 68 to go with his two 69's.
He lies in fourth place with 206, 10 under par but five strokes behind Singh.
